name: Vandervell
context: Entered the Ferrari 375 that Piero Taruffi took to victory in the 1952 Ulster Trophy.

name: Ecurie Ecosse
context: Entered the Jaguar D-Type in which Desmond Titterington was fastest finisher at the May 1955 Ulster Trophy.

name: Aston Martin
context: A recurring British works entry; Collins and Griffith's 1953 TT win came in the works DB3S.

name: Scuderia Ferrari
context: The 750 Monza of Hawthorn and Trintignant took the 1954 TT scratch and championship result.

name: Mercedes-Benz
context: The 300 SLR team of the 1955 TT; Moss and Fitch won the final Dundrod car race in a 300 SLR.

name: Jaguar (works)
context: A single factory D-Type, shared by Mike Hawthorn and Desmond Titterington, challenged the Mercedes team in the 1955 TT until mechanical failure late in the race.

name: BRM
context: Brought the experimental V16 for Moss and Fangio at the 1952 Ulster Trophy; neither finished.

name: Alfa Romeo
context: The reigning World Champions' team: Farina's 1951 Ulster Trophy win and lap record came in the works 159 'Alfetta'.

name: Maserati
context: Two works 3-litre cars for Behra, Musso, Bordoni and Musy joined the 1955 Tourist Trophy entry.

name: Porsche
context: The official Porsche team raced in the 1955 Tourist Trophy; Masten Gregory was loaned to it after Gendebien's Wheeler's Corner crash.

name: DB (Deutsch & Bonnet)
context: The small Panhard-powered DBs whose handicap victory gave Laureau and Armagnac the 1954 Tourist Trophy.

name: Enrico Platé
context: Entered a Maserati 4CLT at the 1951 Ulster Trophy meeting — the entry survives in the photographic archive, its driver unconfirmed.
